items.prompt: The white bishop gives check. Tap every square where the black king could step to get out of check.

claims.statement: Black is in check.
The king has exactly four legal squares.

hints: The bishop attacks along one diagonal. Which squares near the king does that diagonal touch?
The king may not step onto a square the bishop attacks, and may not stay where it is.
Check every square beside the king, one at a time. Is each attacked by the bishop?
items.explain: The bishop attacks the king along the diagonal and also covers the square d7, so the king may not go there. The other four squares around the king are free, and stepping to any of them ends the check.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is it check, checkmate or neither?

claims.statement: Black is checkmated.
One white piece attacks the king.

hints: Is the king attacked right now? Follow each straight line and each diagonal that ends on the king.
If the king is attacked: can the checker be taken, can something go in the way, can the king step to a safe square?
Any one of those that works makes it only check. If none works, it is checkmate.
items.explain: The rook checks along the eighth row. The king's own pawns fill the squares in front of it, the rook covers the only other square, and nothing can take the rook or step in the way. Checkmate.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is it check, checkmate or neither?

claims.statement: Black is not in check and has legal moves.
No white piece attacks the king.

hints: Is the king attacked right now? Follow each straight line and each diagonal that ends on the king.

items.explain: The knight on d7 stands on the bishop's line, so the bishop does not attack the king. Black is not in check, and it has legal moves.
